subject.title: fix: stabilize embedded prompt caching across policy and Responses boundaries

question: Should denied senders continue seeing protected core-tool schemas when every invocation is blocked by immutable turn policy before hooks and side effects?
rationale: The PR deliberately moves the boundary from schema visibility to execution authorization to preserve prompt-cache shape; automated review can validate enforcement but cannot choose that product security posture.

options.title: Approve visible schemas
options.body: Accept stable protected-tool visibility with mandatory fail-closed authorization before hooks, implementations, and side effects across every runtime.

options.title: Retain hidden schemas
options.body: Keep sender-dependent catalogues and reject this cache-stability tradeoff for protected tools.

recommendation.title: Approve visible schemas
recommendation.body: Accept stable protected-tool visibility with mandatory fail-closed authorization before hooks, implementations, and side effects across every runtime.

likelyOwner.reason: His history spans the Codex lifecycle and gateway loopback/tool-resolution boundaries where this product security decision lands.
